selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This MemorySSA fix corrects clobber-walker handling of loop-carried dependencies for calls. It propagates the MayBeCrossIteration state when extending MemoryPhi search paths, applies BatchAACrossIterationScope during clobber sanity checking, and adds a MemorySSA walker regression test requiring an exit-block memcpy to be clobbered by the loop MemoryPhi rather than liveOnEntry.
Changed symbols: ClobberWalker; ClobberWalker::addSearches; ClobberWalker::DefPath; checkClobberSanity; BatchAACrossIterationScope; MemoryAccessPair; ConstMemoryAccessPair
Behavioral change: Cross-iteration state is propagated into paused and resumed MemoryPhi search paths instead of being omitted when searches are added.; The clobber sanity check performs alias/clobber queries under BatchAACrossIterationScope using the path's MayBeCrossIteration state.; The walker is tested to select a loop MemoryPhi, rather than liveOnEntry, as the clobber for an exiting memcpy that depends on loop-carried stores.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA.cpp; ClobberWalker
Reproducer link: The added regression has a loop MemoryPhi fed by a loop store and an exit-block llvm.memcpy, and checks that the memcpy is clobbered by the MemoryPhi rather than liveOnEntry.
Pass or subsystem link: MemorySSA; MemorySSA clobber walker; MemorySSA clobber sanity verification
Causal explanation: This is a direct match to the issue's subsystem and failure mode: an incorrect clobber-walker result across a loop can make MemorySSA dependency reasoning inconsistent and trigger verification failures. The visible changes specifically alter cross-iteration aliasing and MemoryPhi path handling, while the new test validates the relevant clobber result for a call-like memory operation. diff --git a/llvm/test/Analysis/MemorySSA/call-loop-carried-dependency.ll b/llvm/test/Analysis/MemorySSA/call-loop-carried-dependency.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..c27de9f79814
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Analysis/MemorySSA/call-loop-carried-dependency.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --check-inst-comments --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='print<memoryssa-walker>' -disable-output < %s 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+
+; Make sure that the memcpy is clobbered by the memoryphi, not by liveOnEntry.
+define void @test(i1 %c, ptr %path, ptr %name) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @test(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[C:%.*]], ptr [[PATH:%.*]], ptr [[NAME:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP:%.*]] = alloca [260 x i8], align 16
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[WHILE_BODY:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[WHILE_BODY]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  ; 3 = MemoryPhi({entry,liveOnEntry},{while.body,1})
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[IV_NEXT:%.*]], %[[WHILE_BODY]] ], [ 259, %[[ENTRY]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IV_NEXT]] = add nsw i64 [[IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_IV:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds [260 x i8], ptr [[TMP]], i64 0, i64 [[IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:  ; 1 = MemoryDef(3)->3 - clobbered by 3 = MemoryPhi({entry,liveOnEntry},{while.body,1})
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i8 42, ptr [[TMP_IV]], align 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[C]], label %[[WHILE_BODY]], label %[[EXIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_IV_1:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr [[TMP_IV]], i64 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SUB7:%.*]] = sub nsw i64 259, [[IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:  ; 2 = MemoryDef(1)->3 - clobbered by 3 = MemoryPhi({entry,liveOnEntry},{while.body,1})
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 1 [[NAME]], ptr nonnull align 1 [[TMP_IV_1]], i64 [[SUB7]], i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %tmp = alloca [260 x i8], align 16
+  br label %while.body
+
+while.body:
+  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.next, %while.body ], [ 259, %entry ]
+  %iv.next = add nsw i64 %iv, -1
+  %tmp.iv = getelementptr inbounds [260 x i8], ptr %tmp, i64 0, i64 %iv
+  store i8 42, ptr %tmp.iv, align 1
+  br i1 %c, label %while.body, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  %tmp.iv.1 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %tmp.iv, i64 1
+  %sub7 = sub nsw i64 259, %iv
+  call void @llvm.memcpy(ptr align 1 %name, ptr nonnull align 1 %tmp.iv.1, i64 %sub7, i1 false)
+  ret void
+}

top_candidates.subject: [Transforms/Scalar][NFC] Drop uses of BranchInst (#186592)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This NFC-labeled Scalar-transforms change replaces generic BranchInst assumptions with CondBrInst or UncondBrInst where a transformation requires that specific form. It affects loop idiom recognition, loop predication, induction-variable exit optimization, jump threading, and DFA jump threading, including CFG-producing code that uses DomTreeUpdater.
Changed symbols: detectPopcountIdiom; detectShiftUntilZeroIdiom; JumpThreadingPass::threadEdge; JumpThreadingPass::tryToUnfoldSelect; LoopPredication::predicateLoopExits; LoopIdiomRecognize::insertFFSIfProfitable; IndVarSimplify::optimizeLoopExits; DFAJumpThreading::unfold
Behavioral change: Several scalar optimizations now proceed only after proving that a terminator is conditional, rather than merely a BranchInst.; DFAJumpThreading::unfold now obtains an UncondBrInst directly when entering its unconditional-start-block path.; Unconditional branch creation in jump threading is represented with UncondBrInst.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSAAnalysis
Pass or subsystem link: Transforms/Scalar; LoopPredication; JumpThreading; DFAJumpThreading
Causal explanation: LoopPredication's visible context constructs a MemorySSAUpdater when MemorySSA is available and preserves MemorySSAAnalysis after a successful transform, so scalar CFG changes are in the broader risk area for MemorySSA consistency. However, the changed lines only refine branch subclasses; they do not alter MemorySSA updates, dominance updates, clobber walking, or verification. The retrieved evidence therefore provides only an indirect connection to the reported assertion.

Summary: This NFC-labeled Transforms/Utils change replaces generic BranchInst creation and result types with CondBrInst or UncondBrInst where the branch form is known. It also changes redirectToHub so that, when only the original conditional branch's successor 1 is redirected, successor 1 is explicitly retargeted to the first guard block instead of falling through to the branch-replacement case.
Changed symbols: redirectToHub; llvm::ConstantFoldTerminator; insertLoopExpansion; llvm::emitAMDGPUPrintfCall; SplitBlockPredecessorsImpl; llvm::UnrollAndJamLoop; SwitchConvert; CondBrInst

Pass or subsystem link: Transforms/Utils; CFG construction and rewriting

Incorrect CFG rewrites can indirectly affect dominance and MemorySSA consumers, but the retrieved hunks contain no MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, clobber-walker, or verification logic, and no reproducer or test tying this guard-block transformation to the reported -O1 crash.

top_candidates.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: LICM's noConflictingReadWrites safety check is changed to skip MemorySSA accesses dominated by the instruction's memory-defining access when considering a non-sink operation. This changes which accesses LICM treats as conflicting during hoist-safety analysis, with accompanying MemorySSA expectation changes and new LICM tests for hoisting calls that read or write inaccessible memory.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; MemorySSA::dominates; LICMPass; LNICMPass
Behavioral change: For non-sink motion, noConflictingReadWrites now ignores each candidate MemorySSA access MA when MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA) is true.; LICM may consequently permit hoisting when accesses dominated by IMD are excluded from the conflicting-read/write scan.; The added LICM test distinguishes legal hoisting of an inaccessible-memory writer from a case where a conflicting inaccessible-memory reader prevents hoisting.
Assertion or trace link: MSSA->dominates
Reproducer link: The issue is an optimizer crash at -O1 in MemorySSA clobber-walker verification; this change alters LICM's MemorySSA-based legality reasoning and can change the set of motions and MemorySSA updates performed.; The retrieved tests explicitly exercise loop-mssa(licm) and show changed MemoryDef/MemoryPhi expectations, demonstrating that the change affects MemorySSA-observable structure.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; MemorySSA; MemorySSA dominance reasoning; loop-mssa
Causal explanation: This is a strong candidate because it directly adds an MSSA->dominates decision to LICM's MemorySSA-backed motion-safety logic. The reported assertion involves MemorySSA clobber-walker verification and dominance-related correctness; altered filtering of accesses can lead LICM to make a different motion or expose an invalid MemorySSA state. The retrieved evidence does not prove that this exact change produces OtherClobbers or ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult, so the link is high-risk rather than confirmed.
Causal confidence: 0.74
Build risk: Directly changes a MemorySSA-dependent LICM safety condition.; Preserves MemorySSAAnalysis after LICM/LNICM transformations in the shown pass context, so correctness depends on valid MemorySSA state after changed motion decisions.; Adds dedicated loop-mssa LICM coverage and modifies MemorySSA FileCheck expectations, indicating observable analysis/transform behavior changes.

index 000000000000..55f57367495a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/sdag-extload-combine-crash.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+; This test checks that after SelectionDAG runs, DAGCombiner can combine a
+; load and a zext instruction without crashing in tryToFoldExtOfLoad(),
+; even when the folded load result is still used along the truncate
+; replacement path.
+
+; RUN: llc -O3 -mtriple=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -filetype=null < %s
+
+@ak = external global i16
+@s = external global i16
+
+define i32 @main() {
+entry:
+  %0 = load i16, ptr @ak, align 2
+  %1 = load volatile i16, ptr @s, align 2
+  %2 = load i16, ptr @ak, align 2
+  %3 = xor i16 %2, -1
+  %conv4211404 = zext i16 %3 to i64
+  %xor422 = xor i64 1, %conv4211404
+  %conv3591399 = zext i16 %0 to i64
+  %or424 = or i64 %xor422, %conv3591399
+  %conv333 = sext i16 %0 to i32
+  %conv434 = zext i16 %2 to i32
+  %4 = trunc i64 %or424 to i32
+  %or436 = or i32 %conv434, %4
+  %conv453 = xor i32 %conv333, %or436
+  ret i32 %conv453
+}

evidence: Directly changes LICM MemorySSA legality logic using the exact reported mechanism, MSSA->dominates, to prune accesses during conflict analysis.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The commit changes LICM's MemorySSA-backed noConflictingReadWrites check so that, while evaluating a hoist rather than a sink, MemorySSA accesses dominated by the instruction's MemoryDef are skipped before conflict analysis. It directly changes how LICM interprets MemorySSA dominance during motion-safety decisions, with tests updating MemorySSA graphs and adding inaccessible-memory call hoisting cases.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; LoopInvariantCodeMotion; LICMPass; LNICMPass; MemorySSA::dominates
Behavioral change: For non-sinking LICM decisions, skips a candidate MemorySSA access when MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA) is true.; Changes the set of MemorySSA accesses considered as possible read/write conflicts before hoisting.; Enables or changes LICM hoisting decisions for inaccessible-memory calls, while retaining a negative case where an inaccessible-memory reader prevents hoisting.; Updates expected MemorySSA MemoryPhi/MemoryDef structure in analysis tests.

+  %conv333 = sext i16 %0 to i32
+  %conv434 = zext i16 %2 to i32
+  %4 = trunc i64 %or424 to i32
+  %or436 = or i32 %conv434, %4

top_candidates.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The commit changes LICM's MemorySSA-backed noConflictingReadWrites check so that, while evaluating a hoist rather than a sink, MemorySSA accesses dominated by the instruction's MemoryDef are skipped before conflict analysis. It directly changes how LICM interprets MemorySSA dominance during motion-safety decisions, with tests updating MemorySSA graphs and adding inaccessible-memory call hoisting cases.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; LoopInvariantCodeMotion; LICMPass; LNICMPass; MemorySSA::dominates
Behavioral change: For non-sinking LICM decisions, skips a candidate MemorySSA access when MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA) is true.; Changes the set of MemorySSA accesses considered as possible read/write conflicts before hoisting.; Enables or changes LICM hoisting decisions for inaccessible-memory calls, while retaining a negative case where an inaccessible-memory reader prevents hoisting.; Updates expected MemorySSA MemoryPhi/MemoryDef structure in analysis tests.
Assertion or trace link: MSSA.dominates
Reproducer link: The new LICM test exercises MemorySSA-backed loop hoisting of calls with inaccessible-memory effects, a memory-dependence scenario related to optimizer reasoning.; The retrieved evidence does not include the reported reduced C testcase, an -O1 invocation, OtherClobbers, ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult, or the asserted condition.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; MemorySSA; MemorySSA-backed scalar optimization; loop-mssa
Causal explanation: This is a strong subsystem match because it directly introduces an MSSA->dominates-based pruning rule in LICM's MemorySSA conflict walk. If the new skip condition incorrectly excludes a required clobber/conflict or relies on an invalid dominance relationship after transformation, LICM could make a different motion decision and expose inconsistency to later MemorySSA verification. However, the retrieved hunks do not show any modification to MemorySSA.cpp or ClobberWalker itself, so the exact reported OtherClobbers/verifyOptResult failure remains unproven.
Causal confidence: 0.72
Build risk: Directly changes MemorySSA-based legality logic in the scalar LICM pass.; Adds a loop-mssa LICM regression test covering inaccessible-memory calls and positive/negative hoisting outcomes.; Updates expected MemorySSA MemoryPhi and MemoryDef output in existing analysis tests.; No retrieved test specifically runs the reported reduced reproducer under -O1 with MemorySSA verification enabled.

+; This test checks that after SelectionDAG runs, DAGCombiner can combine a
+; load and a zext instruction without crashing in tryToFoldExtOfLoad(),
+; even when the folded load result is still used along the truncate
+; replacement path.
+
+; RUN: llc -O3 -mtriple=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -filetype=null < %s
+
+@ak = external global i16
+@s = external global i16
+
+define i32 @main() {
+entry:
+  %0 = load i16, ptr @ak, align 2
+  %1 = load volatile i16, ptr @s, align 2
+  %2 = load i16, ptr @ak, align 2
+  %3 = xor i16 %2, -1
+  %conv4211404 = zext i16 %3 to i64
+  %xor422 = xor i64 1, %conv4211404
+  %conv3591399 = zext i16 %0 to i64
+  %or424 = or i64 %xor422, %conv3591399
+  %conv333 = sext i16 %0 to i32
+  %conv434 = zext i16 %2 to i32
+  %4 = trunc i64 %or424 to i32
+  %or436 = or i32 %conv434, %4
+  %conv453 = xor i32 %conv333, %or436
+  ret i32 %conv453
+}

--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopTransformWarning/vectorizer-loop-kind-unroll-warning.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='loop-vectorize,loop-unroll,transform-warning' \
+; RUN:   -force-vector-width=4 -force-vector-interleave=1 \
+; RUN:   -enable-epilogue-vectorization -epilogue-vectorization-force-VF=4 \
+; RUN:   -disable-output -pass-remarks-missed=transform-warning 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='loop-vectorize,loop-unroll,transform-warning' \
+; RUN:   -force-vector-width=4 -force-vector-interleave=1 \
+; RUN:   -enable-epilogue-vectorization -epilogue-vectorization-force-VF=4 \
+; RUN:   -disable-output -pass-remarks-output=%t.yaml 2>&1
+; RUN: FileCheck --input-file=%t.yaml %s --check-prefix=YAML
+
+; Verify that when the loop vectorizer produces body / epilogue
+; metadata and the unroller *fails* to unroll (runtime unrolling is disabled),
+; the surviving unroll hints reach WarnMissedTransforms, which emits a
+; distinct "not unrolled" warning for each loop-kind qualifier.
+;
+; Pipeline: loop-vectorize -> loop-unroll -> transform-warning.
+; Epilogue vectorization is forced to exercise all four loop categories:
+;
+;   1. plain loop         – not touched by the vectorizer
+;   2. vectorized loop    – main vector body      (has vectorize.body)
+;   3. epilogue loop      – epilogue loop          (has vectorize.epilogue)
+;
+; Runtime unrolling is disabled via metadata so the unroller cannot act,
+; causing the pragma-unroll hint to survive to the warning pass.
+; Both stderr warnings and YAML structured output are checked.
+
+;--- plain_loop: vectorize.enable=false, runtime unroll disabled ---------------
+
+; CHECK:     warning: test.cpp:1:1: loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+; CHECK-NOT: warning: test.cpp:1:1: vectorized
+; CHECK-NOT: warning: test.cpp:1:1: epilogue
+
+define void @plain_loop(ptr noalias %A, i64 %n) !dbg !100 {
+entry:
+  br label %loop, !dbg !108
+loop:
+  %i = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%i.next, %loop]

+; RUN:   -disable-output -pass-remarks-output=%t.yaml 2>&1

+exit:

+}

+
+define void @vectorizable_loop(ptr noalias %A, ptr noalias %B, i64 %n) !dbg !200 {
+entry:
+  br label %loop, !dbg !208
+loop:
+  %i = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%i.next, %loop]
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i64 %i
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i64 %i

+  %add = add i32 %v, 1
+  store i32 %add, ptr %gep.b, align 4
+  %i.next = add nuw nsw i64 %i, 1
+  %cmp = icmp slt i64 %i.next, %n

+  ret void
+}

It removes custom DenseMapInfo::getTombstoneKey implementations for ModelledPHI, Expression, EqualBBWrapper, FrozenIndPHIInfo, and UnrolledInstState, and removes tombstone recognition from EarlyCSE's SimpleValue and Local.cpp's PHI sentinel wrapper. The stated intent is removal of unused tombstone-key support rather than a change to memory-dependence algorithms.

new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..eb2c4844c1c8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/AssignGUID.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+//===-- AssignGUID.cpp - Unique identifier assignment pass ------*- C++ -*-===//
+//
+// Part of the LLVM Project, under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions.
+// See https://llvm.org/LICENSE.txt for license information.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+//
+// This file provides a pass which assigns GUID (globally unique identifier)
+// metadata to every GlobalValue in the module, according to its current name,
+// linkage, and originating file. It is idempotent -- if GUID metadata is
+// already present, it does nothing.
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+
+#include "llvm/Transforms/Utils/AssignGUID.h"
+#include "llvm/Support/Debug.h"
+
+using namespace llvm;
+
+void AssignGUIDPass::runOnModule(Module &M) {
+  for (auto &GV : M.globals()) {
+    if (GV.isDeclaration())
+      continue;
+    GV.assignGUID();
+  }
+  for (auto &F : M.functions()) {
+    if (F.isDeclaration())
+      continue;
+    F.assignGUID();
+  }
+}

+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py
+; RUN: opt -passes=instcombine -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+; Pattern: shl X, sub(Y, xor(ctlz(X), BitWidth-1))
+; When BitWidth is a power of 2 and Y < BitWidth-1, the result has its MSB
+; at bit Y: bit Y is set and bits above Y are clear.
+
+define i32 @msb_at_14_bit_set(i32 %x) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @msb_at_14_bit_set(
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 16384
+;
+  %c = call i32 @llvm.ctlz.i32(i32 %x, i1 true)
+  %xored = xor i32 %c, 31
+  %shamt = sub i32 14, %xored
+  %s = shl i32 %x, %shamt
+  %r = and i32 %s, 16384
+  ret i32 %r
+}
+
+define i32 @msb_at_14_high_bits_clear(i32 %x) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @msb_at_14_high_bits_clear(
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 0
+;
+  %c = call i32 @llvm.ctlz.i32(i32 %x, i1 true)
+  %xored = xor i32 %c, 31
+  %shamt = sub i32 14, %xored
+  %s = shl i32 %x, %shamt
+  %r = and i32 %s, 4294934528
+  ret i32 %r
+}
+
+define <2 x i32> @msb_at_14_vec(<2 x i32> %x) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @msb_at_14_vec(
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret <2 x i32> splat (i32 16384)
+;
+  %c = call <2 x i32> @llvm.ctlz.v2i32(<2 x i32> %x, i1 true)
+  %xored = xor <2 x i32> %c, <i32 31, i32 31>
+  %shamt = sub <2 x i32> <i32 14, i32 14>, %xored
+  %s = shl <2 x i32> %x, %shamt
+  %r = and <2 x i32> %s, <i32 16384, i32 16384>
+  ret <2 x i32> %r
+}
+
+; Negative: Y is not less than BitWidth - 1
+define i32 @neg_y_too_large(i32 %x) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @neg_y_too_large(
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[C:%.*]] = call range(i32 0, 33) i32 @llvm.ctlz.i32(i32 [[X:%.*]], i1 true)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[S:%.*]] = shl i32 [[X]], [[C]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[R:%.*]] = and i32 [[S]], -2147483648
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[R]]
+;
+  %c = call i32 @llvm.ctlz.i32(i32 %x, i1 true)
+  %xored = xor i32 %c, 31
+  %shamt = sub i32 31, %xored
+  %s = shl i32 %x, %shamt
+  %r = and i32 %s, 2147483648
+  ret i32 %r
+}
+
+; Negative: BitWidth not a power of two
+define i31 @neg_bad_width(i31 %x) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @neg_bad_width(
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[C:%.*]] = call range(i31 0, 32) i31 @llvm.ctlz.i31(i31 [[X:%.*]], i1 true)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[XORED:%.*]] = xor i31 [[C]], 30
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SHAMT:%.*]] = sub nsw i31 14, [[XORED]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[S:%.*]] = shl i31 [[X]], [[SHAMT]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[R:%.*]] = and i31 [[S]], 16384
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i31 [[R]]

Summary: This commit narrows and separates handling of llvm.assume operand-bundle knowledge. PredicateInfoBuilder::processAssume now recognizes only BundleAttr::NonNull bundles through getBundleAttrFromOBU/getAssumeNonNullInfo rather than processing generic retained knowledge from bundle_op_infos. The predicate representation and printing are switched from Attribute::AttrKind to BundleAttr for bundle assumptions; AssumeBundleBuilder no longer provides the hidden override that preserved all attributes and always filters to useful attributes; and the shown LazyValueInfo logic removes its Attribute::Dereferenceable handling in this assume/guard-range path.
Changed symbols: PredicateInfoBuilder::processAssume; PredicateBundleAssume; PredicateBase::getConstraint; AssumeBuilderState; ShouldPreserveAllAttributes; LazyValueInfoImpl::intersectAssumeOrGuardBlockValueConstantRange; getBundleAttrFromOBU; getAssumeNonNullInfo

Summary: This commit reverts LICM support for hoisting an InsertElementInst past a chain of non-hoistable InsertElementInsts. It removes the insertion-index helper, the chain-reordering transformation, its use-replacement and operand rewiring, and the hoistRegion dispatch that invoked the transformation through LICM's normal hoisting path.
Changed symbols: llvm::hoistRegion; hoistInsertPastInsert; getConstantInsertionIndex; InsertElementInst; MemorySSAUpdater
Behavioral change: LICM no longer canonicalizes nested insertelement chains by moving an outer invariant insertion ahead of inner loop-variant insertions.; LICM no longer rewrites insertelement use-def chains with replaceAllUsesWith, moveBefore, and operand substitution before calling hoist.; The removed path would have called LICM's hoist routine with a MemorySSAUpdater, so this commit eliminates that particular IR-motion and MemorySSA-update path.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: ConstantHoisting now ignores PHI incoming edges whose predecessor blocks are unreachable from the entry block while collecting constant-hoisting candidates. The change prevents candidate/use accounting and insertion-point logic from considering CFG edges that cannot execute; accompanying tests convert a prior assertion-crash test into a passing test and add coverage for unreachable PHI predecessors.
Changed symbols: ConstantHoistingPass::collectConstantCandidates
Behavioral change: For a PHI operand, candidate collection obtains the corresponding incoming block and skips that operand when DominatorTree::isReachableFromEntry reports the predecessor as unreachable.; ConstantHoisting no longer attempts to rebase or account for constants on unreachable PHI edges.; The existing X86 regression changes from expecting an assertion crash to requiring successful ConstantHoisting output; a new AArch64 test covers unreachable PHI edges.
Assertion or trace link: assertion failures; DominatorTree reachability
Reproducer link: The added regression specifically concerns PHIs with incoming edges from blocks having no predecessors and reports prior assertion failures about rebased/user counts.; The issue reproducer instead crashes in MemorySSA ClobberWalker verification with OtherClobbers and MSSA.dominates.
Pass or subsystem link: ConstantHoisting; DominatorTree; Scalar transforms
Causal explanation: There is a weak structural connection through unreachable CFG predecessors and dominance-sensitive optimization behavior, but the retrieved implementation changes only ConstantHoisting candidate collection. It neither touches MemorySSA nor contains ClobberWalker, OtherClobbers, MemorySSA verification, or MemorySSA update logic. The documented assertion is a ConstantHoisting use-rebasing assertion, not the reported MemorySSA assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.13
Build risk: Changes an assertion-regression test into a normal successful opt/FileCheck test, indicating the targeted ConstantHoisting crash is expected to be fixed.; Adds targeted unreachable-PHI coverage on AArch64.; The implementation change is localized to candidate filtering and has no visible MemorySSA API or verification-test coverage.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/ConstantHoisting/AArch64/consthoist-unreachable-phi-edge.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/ConstantHoisting/AArch64/consthoist-unreachable-phi-edge.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..65bce13bf022
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/ConstantHoisting/AArch64/consthoist-unreachable-phi-edge.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt < %s -mtriple aarch64-- -passes=consthoist -S | FileCheck %s
+
+; The PHI node has some inbound edges with constants that originate from
+; basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry. Those could be tricky
+; to update when trying to find insertion points etc for a common base
+; constant.
+
+; The test case was added as a regression test to show that that we no longer
+; hit assertion failures about number of users updated/rebased. The workaround
+; is to ignore phi edges from basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry
+; when looking for candidate constants.
+
+define i64 @func(i1 %b0, i1 %b1) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @func(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[B0:%.*]], i1 [[B1:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B0]], label %[[BLOCK1:.*]], label %[[BLOCK2:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK1]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST1:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK2]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B1]], label %[[BLOCK3:.*]], label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK3]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE1:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE2:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[MERGE]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE1]] ], [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE2]] ], [ [[CONST1]], %[[BLOCK1]] ], [ [[CONST]], %[[BLOCK3]] ], [ 0, %[[BLOCK2]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[V]]
+;
+entry:
+  br i1 %b0, label %block1, label %block2
+
+block1:
+  br label %merge
+
+block2:
+  br i1 %b1, label %block3, label %merge
+
+block3:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable1:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable2:
+  br label %merge
+
+merge:
+  %v = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %unreachable1 ], [ 4886718345, %unreachable2 ], [ 4886718345, %block1 ], [ 4886718345, %block3 ], [ 0, %block2 ]
+  ret i64 %v
+}
+
+

+; RUN: llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv-unknown-unknown %s -o - | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: %if spirv-tools %{ llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv-unknown-unknown %s -o - -filetype=obj | spirv-val %}
+
+; CHECK-DAG: %[[#int8:]] = OpTypeInt 8 0
+; CHECK-DAG: %[[#bool:]] = OpTypeBool
+; CHECK-DAG: %[[#int32:]] = OpTypeInt 32 0
+; CHECK-DAG: %[[#size:]] = OpConstant %[[#int32]] 8
+; CHECK-DAG: %[[#bytearr:]] = OpTypeArray %[[#int8]] %[[#size]]
+; CHECK-DAG: %[[#boolarr:]] = OpTypeArray %[[#bool]] %[[#size]]
+; CHECK-DAG: %[[#boolptr:]] = OpTypePointer Function %[[#boolarr]]
+; CHECK-DAG: %[[#i8ptr:]] = OpTypePointer Function %[[#int8]]
+; CHECK-DAG: %[[#one:]] = OpConstant %[[#]] 1
+
+@bytes = internal global [8 x i8] zeroinitializer
+@bools = internal global [8 x i1] zeroinitializer
+
+; Byte addressing into a byte array lowers to a valid logical access chain.
+; CHECK: OpFunction
+; CHECK: %[[#var:]] = OpVariable %[[#]] Function
+; CHECK: %[[#]] = OpInBoundsAccessChain %[[#i8ptr]] %[[#var]] %[[#one]]
+define void @byte_array() {
+entry:
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr @bytes, i32 1
+  store i8 0, ptr %gep
+  ret void
+}
+
+; Byte addressing into a subbyte array uses the element alloc size as the
+; stride. This previously crashed with a division by zero because the element
+; type size in bits (1 for i1) is not a whole number of bytes.
+; CHECK: OpFunction
+; CHECK: %[[#bvar:]] = OpVariable %[[#boolptr]] Function
+; CHECK: %[[#]] = OpInBoundsAccessChain %[[#]] %[[#bvar]] %[[#one]]
+define void @subbyte_array() {
+entry:
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr @bools, i32 1
+  store i1 true, ptr %gep
+  ret void
+}

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit fixes a LoopInterchange crash in moveLCSSAPhis when followLCSSA returns a non-instruction value, such as a constant. It replaces an unconditional cast<Instruction> with dyn_cast<Instruction> and treats a non-instruction result as a PHI that must be skipped, with a regression test covering a constant-rooted LCSSA use-def chain.
Changed symbols: moveLCSSAPhis; followLCSSA; LoopInterchange; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/lcssa-incoming-value-is-not-instr.ll
Behavioral change: LoopInterchange no longer asserts when followLCSSA returns a constant instead of an Instruction.; moveLCSSAPhis now skips candidate PHIs whose followed incoming value is not an instruction, in addition to skipping values defined in disallowed inner-loop blocks.; The added test verifies interchange can process LCSSA PHIs whose incoming-value chain terminates at a constant.

Reproducer link: Both this commit and the issue concern optimizer crashes, but this commit's reproducer is specifically a constant returned from followLCSSA during LoopInterchange.; The issue reproducer instead crashes during MemorySSA clobber-walker verification at -O1.

+; Ensure that we can handle LCSSA PHI even if the root of the use-def chain of
+; the incoming value is not an instruction.
+
+define i32 @g() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @g() {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER_PREHEADER:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ], [ 0, %[[OUTER_HEADER_PREHEADER]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[TMP1:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH_SPLIT:.*]] ], [ 0, %[[INNER_HEADER_PREHEADER]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER_PREHEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[X:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 42, %[[OUTER_HEADER]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT:%.*]] = add i64 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EC_J:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[J_NEXT]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_EXIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[X_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[X]], %[[OUTER_LATCH]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1]] = add i64 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP2:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[TMP1]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[TMP2]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add i64 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EC_I:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[I_NEXT]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EC_I]], label %[[INNER_LATCH_SPLIT]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[X_FINAL:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[X_LCSSA]], %[[INNER_LATCH_SPLIT]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[X_FINAL]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %i = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %i.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br label %inner.header
+
+inner.header:
+  %j = phi i64 [ 0, %outer.header ], [ %j.next, %inner.latch ]
+  br label %inner.latch
+
+inner.latch:
+  %x = phi i32 [ 42, %inner.header ]
+  %j.next = add i64 %j, 1
+  %ec.j = icmp eq i64 %j.next, 2
+  br i1 %ec.j, label %inner.exit, label %inner.header
+
+inner.exit:
+  %x.lcssa = phi i32 [ %x, %inner.latch ]
+  br label %outer.latch
+
+outer.latch:
+  %x.lcssa2 = phi i32 [ %x.lcssa, %inner.exit ]
+  %i.next = add i64 %i, 1
+  %ec.i = icmp eq i64 %i.next, 2

+

+  %x.final = phi i32 [ %x.lcssa2, %outer.latch ]

+}

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This NFC API refactoring adds an isDereferenceablePointer overload that accepts an explicit APInt byte size and implements it as an alignment-1 wrapper around isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointer. MemCpyOptimizer, SimplifyLibCalls, and MergeICmps are migrated from explicit Align(1) calls to the new wrapper, preserving the underlying dereferenceability analysis and its SimplifyQuery context.
Changed symbols: llvm::isDereferenceablePointer; llvm::isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointer; MemCpyOptPass::performCallSlotOptzn; canTransformToMemCmp; BCECmpChain::isDereferenceable; llvm/include/llvm/Analysis/Loads.h; llvm/lib/Analysis/Loads.cpp
Behavioral change: Adds a size-based isDereferenceablePointer API that is explicitly equivalent to isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointer with Align(1).; Updates callers in MemCpyOptimizer, SimplifyLibCalls, and MergeICmps to use the new wrapper instead of spelling Align(1) directly.; The visible implementation delegates directly to the pre-existing aligned dereferenceability routine, retaining its SimplifyQuery, dominance/context, and free-safety reasoning.
Assertion or trace link: MSSA.dominates; MemorySSA; ClobberWalker; verifyOptResult
Reproducer link: The issue concerns an -O1 MemorySSA clobber-walker verification assertion.; This commit affects dereferenceability queries used by memory-related scalar optimizations, but the visible patch presents the change as NFC and preserves the previous Align(1) semantics.
Pass or subsystem link: Analysis/Loads; MemCpyOptimizer; MergeICmps; SimplifyLibCalls; LLVM scalar optimizations
Causal explanation: Dereferenceability decisions can influence whether memory optimizations are enabled, so the migrated MemCpyOptimizer and MergeICmps call sites are superficially relevant to optimizer memory reasoning. However, the new overload is a direct forwarding wrapper to the exact prior isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointer call with alignment 1, and no MemorySSA construction, update, dominance, clobber-walking, or verifier logic changes in the retrieved hunks. The evidence therefore supports only a weak indirect association, not a substantive cause of the reported assertion.

@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+! Each sub-file exercises a different unstructured-CFG pattern inside an
+! `acc loop` whose default parallelism resolves to `independent`.
+
+! RUN: split-file %s %t
+! RUN: %not_todo_cmd bbc -fopenacc -emit-hlfir %t/goto_one_level.f90 -o - 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=GOTO1
+! RUN: %not_todo_cmd bbc -fopenacc -emit-hlfir %t/goto_with_intermediate.f90 -o - 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=GOTO2
+! RUN: %not_todo_cmd bbc -fopenacc -emit-hlfir %t/collapse_cycle.f90 -o - 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=CCYCLE
+! RUN: %not_todo_cmd bbc -fopenacc -emit-hlfir %t/cache_exit.f90 -o - 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=CEXIT
+! RUN: %not_todo_cmd bbc -fopenacc -emit-hlfir %t/cache_select_case.f90 -o - 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=CCASE
+
+!--- goto_one_level.f90
+
+! GOTO exits the inner `acc loop seq` (one level), landing in the body of
+! the outer `acc loop gang vector`. Outer loop defaults to `independent`.
+subroutine test_unstructured6(N, A, B)
+  implicit real*8 (a-h, o-z)
+  !$acc routine gang
+  dimension A(*), B(*)
+  !$acc loop gang vector
+  do 100 i = 1, N
+  !$acc loop seq
+    do 10 j = 1, 1000
+      if (A(i) .gt. B(i)) goto 20
+10  continue
+20  B(i) = A(i)
+100 continue
+end subroutine
+
+! GOTO1: not yet implemented: unstructured do loop in independent OpenACC loop construct
+
+!--- goto_with_intermediate.f90
+
+! Same as above but with intermediate code between the inner loop end and
+! the GOTO target, exercising the jump-table dispatch path.
+subroutine test_unstructured7(A, B, C, N)
+  implicit real*8 (a-h, o-z)
+  !$acc routine gang
+  dimension A(*), B(*), C(*)
+  !$acc loop gang vector
+  do 100 i = 1, N
+  !$acc loop seq
+    do 10 j = 1, 1000
+      if (A(i) .gt. B(i)) goto 20
+10  continue
+    C(i) = 999.0
+20  B(i) = A(i)
+100 continue
+end subroutine
+
+! GOTO2: not yet implemented: unstructured do loop in independent OpenACC loop construct
+
+!--- collapse_cycle.f90
+
+! Orphan `acc loop collapse(2)` with an early-exit (CYCLE) - defaults to
+! `independent` inside the (non-seq) acc routine.
+subroutine test_unstructured_collapse_loop_only(a)
+  !$acc routine gang
+  integer :: i, j, jdiag
+  real(8) :: a(:,:)
+  jdiag = 4
+  !$acc loop collapse(2)
+  do j = 1, 8
+    do i = 1, 8
+      if (i == jdiag) then
+        a(i, j) = 0.0d0
+        cycle
+      end if
+      a(i, j) = real(i + j, 8)
+    end do
+  end do
+end subroutine
+
+! CCYCLE: not yet implemented: unstructured do loop in independent OpenACC loop construct
+
+!--- cache_exit.f90
+
+! `acc loop` with `cache` directive and EXIT inside the body - the EXIT
+! makes the loop unstructured. Orphan loop inside a (non-seq) acc routine
+! defaults to `independent`.
+subroutine test_cache_single_element()
+  !$acc routine gang
+  integer, parameter :: n = 10
+  real, dimension(n) :: a, b
+  integer :: i
+
+  !$acc loop
+  do i = 1, n
+    !$acc cache(b(i))
+    a(i) = b(i)
+    if (a(i) > 100.0) exit
+  end do
+end subroutine
+
+! CEXIT: not yet implemented: unstructured do loop in independent OpenACC loop construct
+
+!--- cache_select_case.f90
+
+! `acc loop` with `cache` directive and SELECT CASE inside the body - the
+! SELECT CASE makes the loop's body have unstructured CFG. Orphan loop
+! inside a (non-seq) acc routine defaults to `independent`.
+subroutine test_cache_nonunit_lb()
+  !$acc routine gang
+  integer :: arr(10:20)
+  integer :: i
+
+  !$acc loop
+  do i = 10, 20
+    !$acc cache(arr(15))
+    select case (mod(i, 3))
+    case (0)
+      arr(i) = i * 2
+    case (1)
+      arr(i) = i * 3
+    case default
+      arr(i) = i
+    end select
+  end do
+end subroutine
+
+! CCASE: not yet implemented: unstructured do loo

steps.subject: [LSR] Narrow search space by merging users outside and inside loop (#202676)

evidence: Adds an LSR heuristic that merges in-loop and outside-loop uses and changes generated memory-address forms.
It can indirectly alter later MemorySSA graphs, but has no direct MemorySSA updater, clobber walker, or dominance-verification logic.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds an LSR search-space narrowing step that tries to merge an LSR use whose fixups are entirely outside a loop into a compatible in-loop use when formula bases and offsets match and the outside-use offset range is legal for every candidate formula. The merge copies fixups to the in-loop use and deletes the outside-loop use. It is invoked from LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceUsingHeuristics only when estimated search-space complexity reaches the configured limit.
Changed symbols: LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceByMergingUsesOutsideLoop; LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceUsingHeuristics; LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceByFilterPostInc; LSRInstance::DeleteUse; LSRUse::pushFixup
Behavioral change: Adds a complexity-triggered preselection heuristic that merges eligible outside-loop LSR uses into in-loop uses rather than retaining them as separate search-space entries.; Requires the outside use to have all fixups outside the loop, a nonempty formula list, and a matching initial formula base/scale/offset description in an in-loop use.; Checks that the outside-use offset range is legal for all formulae of the selected in-loop use before copying fixups and deleting the original use.; Changes the generated loop-strength-reduction choices for loops containing both in-loop and post-loop memory-address uses.
Assertion or trace link: No direct MemorySSA, ClobberWalker, OtherClobbers, or MSSA.dominates assertion term appears in the candidate hunks.; The new X86 regression test explicitly describes preventing an LSR assertion failure caused by an incompatible outside-loop fixup after a merge.
Reproducer link: The added invalid_offset_outside_loop test has a pointer induction variable used in a loop call and then in an exit-block GEP/store, matching the new outside-loop-use merge domain.; The test commentary identifies a failure mode where merging an outside-loop fixup can make previously available formulas illegal.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopStrengthReduce; LLVM scalar optimizations; Indirectly, optimized loop memory-address generation
Causal explanation: This is an O1-relevant scalar loop transformation that can alter the placement and form of generated memory-addressing operations, so it could indirectly change the MemorySSA graph later observed by verification. New X86 and AArch64 loop-reduce tests provide target-specific coverage, but no retrieved test exercises MemorySSA verification.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/use-outside-loop-crash.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/use-outside-loop-crash.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..2fdee2ae94e9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/use-outside-loop-crash.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,165 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -mtriple=x86_64 -loop-reduce -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+declare i1 @otherfn(ptr)
+
+; The use of %ptr in %gep outside the loop uses a fixup of 8 which is
+; incompatible with the use inside the loop as an argument to a call. We
+; therefore can't merge the two, as it would cause an assertion failure.
+
+define i64 @invalid_offset_outside_loop(ptr %ptr.arg, i64 %iv.arg) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @invalid_offset_outside_loop(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr [[PTR_ARG:%.*]], i64 [[IV_ARG:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = add i64 [[IV_ARG]], -2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], %[[LOOP_INC:.*]] ], [ [[TMP0]], %[[ENTRY]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PTR:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[PTR_ARG]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[PTR_NEXT:%.*]], %[[LOOP_INC]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CALL:%.*]] = call i1 @otherfn(ptr [[PTR]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CALL]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[LOOP_INC]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP_INC]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PTR_NEXT]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 16
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV_NEXT]], -3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND]], label %[[EXIT]], label %[[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp slt i64 [[TMP1]], [[IV_ARG]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP2:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL1:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i64 1, i64 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL2:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP2]], i64 [[SEL1]], i64 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SEL2]], ptr [[GEP]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %ptr = phi ptr [ %ptr.arg, %entry ], [ %ptr.next, %loop.inc ]
+  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.arg, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop.inc ]
+  %call = call i1 @otherfn(ptr %ptr)
+  br i1 %call, label %exit, label %loop.inc
+
+loop.inc:
+  %ptr.next = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 16
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, -1
+  %exitcond = icmp eq i64 %iv, 0
+  br i1 %exitcond, label %exit, label %loop
+
+exit:
+  %cmp1 = icmp slt i64 %iv, %iv.arg
+  %cmp2 = icmp eq i64 %iv, 1
+  %sel1 = select i1 %cmp1, i64 1, i64 2
+  %sel2 = select i1 %cmp2, i64 %sel1, i64 3
+  %gep = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 8
+  store i64 %sel2, ptr %gep, align 8
+  %sub = add i64 %iv, -2
+  ret i64 %sub
+}
+
+; Stream 0 has two in-loop loads at relative offsets {-2^30, 0}, which makes
+; GenerateConstantOffsets produce formulae with BaseOffset +2^30. The exit
+; block loads at +1.5*2^30 past the post-inc pointer; x86 accepts that as a
+; disp32, so the merge gate isLegalUse(LU.MinOffset, LU.MaxOffset, ...,
+; Formulae[0]) passes, but 2^30 + 1.5*2^30 = 2.5*2^30 does not fit in a
+; signed 32-bit displacement, so the +2^30 formulae become illegal once the
+; outside-loop fixup is merged in. The test is sized so that the merge itself
+; drops EstimateSearchSpaceComplexity() below ComplexityLimit, so no later
+; narrowing step deletes the now-illegal formulae before Solve().
+
+define i32 @illegal_formula_after_merge(ptr %p, i64 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @illegal_formula_after_merge(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr [[P:%.*]], i64 [[N:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[P0_LOAD:%.*]] = load ptr, ptr [[P]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ARRAYIDX1:%.*]] = getelementptr ptr, ptr [[P]], i64 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[P1_LOAD:%.*]] = load ptr, pt

; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 2
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp slt i64 [[TMP1]], [[IV_ARG]]
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP2:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL1:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i64 1, i64 2
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL2:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP2]], i64 [[SEL1]], i64 3
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 8
; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SEL2]], ptr [[GEP]], align 8
; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[LSR_IV]]
;
entry:
  br label %loop

loop:
  %ptr = phi ptr [ %ptr.arg, %entry ], [ %ptr.next, %loop.inc ]
  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.arg, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop.inc ]
  %call = call i1 @otherfn(ptr %ptr)

  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, -1
  %exitcond = icmp eq i64 %iv, 0

top_candidates.subject: [LSR] Narrow search space by merging users outside and inside loop (#202676)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds an LSR search-space narrowing step that tries to merge an LSR use whose fixups are entirely outside a loop into a compatible in-loop use when formula bases and offsets match and the outside-use offset range is legal for every candidate formula. The merge copies fixups to the in-loop use and deletes the outside-loop use. It is invoked from LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceUsingHeuristics only when estimated search-space complexity reaches the configured limit.
Changed symbols: LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceByMergingUsesOutsideLoop; LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceUsingHeuristics; LSRInstance::NarrowSearchSpaceByFilterPostInc; LSRInstance::DeleteUse; LSRUse::pushFixup
Behavioral change: Adds a complexity-triggered preselection heuristic that merges eligible outside-loop LSR uses into in-loop uses rather than retaining them as separate search-space entries.; Requires the outside use to have all fixups outside the loop, a nonempty formula list, and a matching initial formula base/scale/offset description in an in-loop use.; Checks that the outside-use offset range is legal for all formulae of the selected in-loop use before copying fixups and deleting the original use.; Changes the generated loop-strength-reduction choices for loops containing both in-loop and post-loop memory-address uses.
Assertion or trace link: No direct MemorySSA, ClobberWalker, OtherClobbers, or MSSA.dominates assertion term appears in the candidate hunks.; The new X86 regression test explicitly describes preventing an LSR assertion failure caused by an incompatible outside-loop fixup after a merge.
Reproducer link: The added invalid_offset_outside_loop test has a pointer induction variable used in a loop call and then in an exit-block GEP/store, matching the new outside-loop-use merge domain.; The test commentary identifies a failure mode where merging an outside-loop fixup can make previously available formulas illegal.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopStrengthReduce; LLVM scalar optimizations; Indirectly, optimized loop memory-address generation
Causal explanation: This is an O1-relevant scalar loop transformation that can alter the placement and form of generated memory-addressing operations, so it could indirectly change the MemorySSA graph later observed by verification. However, the retrieved implementation does not create, update, query, or preserve MemorySSA, and its explicit assertion regression is an LSR formula-legality failure rather than the reported MemorySSA clobber-walker assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.25
Build risk: Adds a new heuristic that mutates the Uses vector while iterating, including explicit index/count adjustment after DeleteUse.; The eligibility check compares only the initial formula for structural compatibility while separately checking legality across all candidate formulae; the added X86 test demonstrates this area already required careful legality handling.; New X86 and AArch64 loop-reduce tests provide target-specific coverage, but no retrieved test exercises MemorySSA verification.

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,165 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -mtriple=x86_64 -loop-reduce -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+declare i1 @otherfn(ptr)
+
+; The use of %ptr in %gep outside the loop uses a fixup of 8 which is
+; incompatible with the use inside the loop as an argument to a call. We
+; therefore can't merge the two, as it would cause an assertion failure.
+
+define i64 @invalid_offset_outside_loop(ptr %ptr.arg, i64 %iv.arg) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @invalid_offset_outside_loop(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr [[PTR_ARG:%.*]], i64 [[IV_ARG:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = add i64 [[IV_ARG]], -2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], %[[LOOP_INC:.*]] ], [ [[TMP0]], %[[ENTRY]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PTR:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[PTR_ARG]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[PTR_NEXT:%.*]], %[[LOOP_INC]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CALL:%.*]] = call i1 @otherfn(ptr [[PTR]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CALL]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[LOOP_INC]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP_INC]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PTR_NEXT]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 16
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV_NEXT]], -3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND]], label %[[EXIT]], label %[[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp slt i64 [[TMP1]], [[IV_ARG]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP2:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL1:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i64 1, i64 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL2:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP2]], i64 [[SEL1]], i64 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SEL2]], ptr [[GEP]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %ptr = phi ptr [ %ptr.arg, %entry ], [ %ptr.next, %loop.inc ]
+  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.arg, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop.inc ]
+  %call = call i1 @otherfn(ptr %ptr)
+  br i1 %call, label %exit, label %loop.inc
+
+loop.inc:
+  %ptr.next = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 16
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, -1
+  %exitcond = icmp eq i64 %iv, 0
+  br i1 %exitcond, label %exit, label %loop
+
+exit:
+  %cmp1 = icmp slt i64 %iv, %iv.arg
+  %cmp2 = icmp eq i64 %iv, 1
+  %sel1 = select i1 %cmp1, i64 1, i64 2
+  %sel2 = select i1 %cmp2, i64 %sel1, i64 3
+  %gep = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 8
+  store i64 %sel2, ptr %gep, align 8
+  %sub = add i64 %iv, -2
+  ret i64 %sub
+}
+
+; Stream 0 has two in-loop loads at relative offsets {-2^30, 0}, which makes
+; GenerateConstantOffsets produce formulae with BaseOffset +2^30. The exit
+; block loads at +1.5*2^30 past the post-inc pointer; x86 accepts that as a
+; disp32, so the merge gate isLegalUse(LU.MinOffset, LU.MaxOffset, ...,
+; Formulae[0]) passes, but 2^30 + 1.5*2^30 = 2.5*2^30 does not fit in a
+; signed 32-bit displacement, so the +2^30 formulae become illegal once the
+; outside-loop fixup is merged in. The test is sized so that the merge itself
+; drops EstimateSearchSpaceComplexity() below ComplexityLimit, so no later
+; narrowing step deletes the now-illegal formulae before Solve().
+
+define i32 @illegal_formula_after_merge(ptr %p, i64 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @illegal_formula_after_merge(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr [[P:%.*]], i64 [[N:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[P0_LOAD:%.*]] = load ptr, ptr [[P]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ARRAYIDX1:%.*]] = getelementptr ptr, ptr [[P]], i64 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[P1_LOAD:%.*]] = load ptr, pt

top_candidates.subject: [SROA] Extend tree-structured merge to handle init + RMW pattern (#194441)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends SROA tree-structured merging from a stores-only layout into an initialization-plus-read-modify-write pattern. It distinguishes optional full-width initialization and final-load operations from partial loads and stores, relaxes accepted loads to simple non-atomic/non-volatile loads, and adds ordering/basic-block constraints so the RMW sequence can be reasoned about without PHIs.
Changed symbols: StoreInfo; LoadInfo; FullLoad; InitStore; IsTypeValidForTreeStructuredMerge
Behavioral change: Separates partial StoreInfos and LoadInfos from an optional full-width InitStore and optional full-width FullLoad.; Accepts simple loads based on type validity rather than requiring every accepted load to be the sole full-width load.; Recognizes an init-plus-partial-load/partial-store RMW form, with at most one full-width init store and one full-width final load.; For the RMW path, requires the init store and all partial loads to be in the same basic block as the partial stores so instruction ordering can be established with comesBefore and no PHIs are needed.; Retains an exact non-overlapping, full-coverage tiling check for the stores-only pattern.
Assertion or trace link: No retrieved hunk contains MemorySSA, ClobberWalker, verifyOptResult, OtherClobbers, or MSSA.dominates.
Reproducer link: The changed logic specifically broadens handling of full-width initialization followed by partial loads and stores, an IR shape involving multiple ordered memory accesses.; No retrieved regression test or function context ties this RMW pattern to the reduced C reproducer for pr204559.
Pass or subsystem link: SROA; LLVM scalar optimizations; Alloca load/store rewriting
Causal explanation: SROA rewrites ordered loads and stores, which is inherently relevant to the memory-dependence graph that MemorySSA verifies. The new RMW recognition path also depends on exact same-block instruction ordering. That makes this a plausible indirect source of an invalid memory-dependence state, but the visible hunks provide no evidence that SROA updates or preserves MemorySSA incorrectly, nor any direct match to the reported clobber-walker trace.
Causal confidence: 0.34
Build risk: The change substantially expands a previously stores-only transformation into a mixed load/store RMW rewrite.; Correctness relies on several newly separated state variables and on ordering checks across InitStore, LoadInfos, and StoreInfos.; No test hunk was retrieved for this candidate, while 78 hunks were omitted; available evidence cannot confirm end-to-end rewrite or verifier coverage.

@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt < %s -mtriple aarch64-- -passes=consthoist -S | FileCheck %s
+
+; The PHI node has some inbound edges with constants that originate from
+; basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry. Those could be tricky
+; to update when trying to find insertion points etc for a common base
+; constant.
+
+; The test case was added as a regression test to show that that we no longer
+; hit assertion failures about number of users updated/rebased. The workaround
+; is to ignore phi edges from basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry
+; when looking for candidate constants.
+
+define i64 @func(i1 %b0, i1 %b1) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @func(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[B0:%.*]], i1 [[B1:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B0]], label %[[BLOCK1:.*]], label %[[BLOCK2:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK1]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST1:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK2]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B1]], label %[[BLOCK3:.*]], label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK3]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE1:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE2:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[MERGE]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE1]] ], [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE2]] ], [ [[CONST1]], %[[BLOCK1]] ], [ [[CONST]], %[[BLOCK3]] ], [ 0, %[[BLOCK2]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[V]]
+;
+entry:
+  br i1 %b0, label %block1, label %block2
+
+block1:
+  br label %merge
+
+block2:
+  br i1 %b1, label %block3, label %merge
+
+block3:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable1:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable2:
+  br label %merge
+
+merge:
+  %v = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %unreachable1 ], [ 4886718345, %unreachable2 ], [ 4886718345, %block1 ], [ 4886718345, %block3 ], [ 0, %block2 ]
+  ret i64 %v
+}

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This SimplifyCFG change makes foldBranchToCommonDest evaluate speculative-execution safety using a concrete predecessor-terminator context and the pass AssumptionCache. It enables context-sensitive speculation only when the folded branch has one predecessor, allowing facts such as dereferenceability attributes or assumes in that predecessor to justify speculative instructions.
Changed symbols: llvm::foldBranchToCommonDest; SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyCondBranch; SimplifyCFGOpt::Options
Behavioral change: foldBranchToCommonDest gains an AssumptionCache parameter.; For exactly one predecessor, the predecessor terminator is passed as the context instruction to isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute.; Speculation safety is now checked with isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute(&I, CxtI, AC), allowing context-sensitive assumptions to affect whether an instruction may be hoisted/speculated.; The added tests show loads becoming speculatable when dereferenceability is available through a parameter attribute or a preceding llvm.assume, while cases without a sufficient context remain unhoisted.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; MSSA.dominates; OtherClobbers
Reproducer link: The issue occurs at -O1 and concerns optimizer memory-dependence verification.; This change can alter -O1 IR by speculating or hoisting loads during SimplifyCFG branch folding.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; LLVM transforms utilities; speculative load motion; MemorySSA consumers after CFG simplification

Such motion can change memory-access placement and the CFG presented to later MemorySSA-based optimizations. However, the retrieved call from simplifyCondBranch explicitly passes MSSAU as nullptr, and no MemorySSA implementation, verifier, or updater logic is changed here. steps.subject: [SimpleLoopUnswitch] Generalize the notion of trivial unswitching (#193989)

evidence: Introduces a new SimpleLoopUnswitch CFG-rewrite path that redirects latch edges, rewrites exit PHIs, and changes predecessor relationships.
Explicitly updates MemorySSA and dominators through MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates, directly matching the reported MSSA dominance and clobber-walker verification failure.
features: dominance-and-phi-maintenance, loop-unswitch-latch-redirection, memoryssa-updater-cfg-update, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The SimpleLoopUnswitch change generalizes trivial unswitching to handle an invariant conditional branch whose successor is a side-effect-free loop latch rather than only a direct loop exit. When the loop has a unique latch exit, loop-exit PHIs are invariant, and ScalarEvolution can prove a finite maximum backedge count, unswitchTrivialBranch redirects the latch edge to the unique latch-exit block, updates exit PHIs, and applies corresponding CFG updates through MemorySSAUpdater or DominatorTree. The existing direct-exit handling is suppressed when this new latch transformation has already modified the branch.
Changed symbols: unswitchTrivialBranch; Loop::getLoopLatch; Loop::getUniqueLatchExitBlock; areLoopExitPHIsLoopInvariant; MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates; DominatorTree::applyUpdates
Behavioral change: Trivial loop unswitching now recognizes a branch-to-latch case when the other successor remains within the loop and the latch has a unique exit.; The transformation replaces a CFG edge from the branch block to the loop latch with an edge to the latch exit, removes the branch block as a latch predecessor, and adds equivalent incoming values to exit PHIs.; The transformation explicitly updates MemorySSA using a Delete edge update for the branch-to-latch edge and an Insert edge update for the branch-to-exit edge when an MSSA updater is available.; The transformation is limited to loops with a computable finite maximum backedge count and a latch containing no side-effecting instructions.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; MSSA.dominates; ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; OtherClobbers; MemorySSA.cpp
Reproducer link: The added/updated phase-ordering test checks changed -O1 CFG output for a nested loop containing loads and stores.; The issue reproduces as an -O1 crash during MemorySSA clobber-walker verification.
Pass or subsystem link: SimpleLoopUnswitch; MemorySSAUpdater; DominatorTree; LLVM scalar optimization pipeline
Causal explanation: This is a strong causal candidate because it introduces a new CFG-rewriting path in SimpleLoopUnswitch that must maintain both dominance and MemorySSA consistency. The new path changes predecessor relationships and PHI inputs while invoking MSSAUpdater::applyUpdates with explicit edge updates. A missing, incomplete, or incorrectly ordered MemorySSA/dominance update for this newly supported latch-to-exit redirection could leave MemorySSA clobber or dominance information inconsistent and plausibly trigger the reported verifier assertion at -O1. The retrieved test also explicitly exercises altered -O1 loop CFG shape with memory accesses, although it does not show the reported assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.78

diff --git a/mlir/lib/Dialect/GPU/Pipelines/GPUToXeVMPipeline.cpp b/mlir/lib/Dialect/GPU/Pipelines/GPUToXeVMPipeline.cpp

@@ -102,0 +103,13 @@ void buildGPUPassPipeline(OpPassManager &pm,
+  // Break down high-level micro-scaling (MX) ops (arith.scaling_extf and
+  // arith.scaling_truncf) into standard arith ops (extf/truncf + mulf), and
+  // expand extf/truncf on f8E8M0FNU into integer bit manipulation. This runs
+  // before the XeVM/LLVM conversions. The f4E2M1FN expansion patterns are

+  // must be expanded here.

+    arithExpandOptions.includeF8E8M0 = true;
+    pm.addNestedPass<gpu::GPUModuleOp>(
+        arith::createArithExpandOpsPass(arithExpandOptions));

--- a/mlir/lib/Dialect/GPU/Pipelines/GPUToXeVMPipeline.cpp
+++ b/mlir/lib/Dialect/GPU/Pipelines/GPUToXeVMPipeline.cpp
@@ -102,0 +103,13 @@ void buildGPUPassPipeline(OpPassManager &pm,
+  // Break down high-level micro-scaling (MX) ops (arith.scaling_extf and
+  // arith.scaling_truncf) into standard arith ops (extf/truncf + mulf), and
+  // expand extf/truncf on f8E8M0FNU into integer bit manipulation. This runs
+  // before the XeVM/LLVM conversions. The f4E2M1FN expansion patterns are
+  // intentionally left disabled: f4E2M1FN extf/truncf are lowered by the XeVM
+  // conversions (xevm.extf), whereas f8E8M0FNU is not supported there and so
+  // must be expanded here.
+  {
+    arith::ArithExpandOpsPassOptions arithExpandOptions;
+    arithExpandOptions.includeF8E8M0 = true;
+    pm.addNestedPass<gpu::GPUModuleOp>(
+        arith::createArithExpandOpsPass(arithExpandOptions));
+  }

diff --git a/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake b/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
index d09def0afdb7..6e56dfd783d1 100644
--- a/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
+++ b/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
@@ -494,0 +495,25 @@ endfunction()
+# PluginManager discovers dynamic script interpreter plugins at runtime by
+# scanning the directory that holds liblldb, so a plugin is loaded only when it
+# sits beside it. A framework build moves liblldb into the bundle, so the plugin
+# must move with it and carry an rpath that reaches liblldb from its new
+# location.
+function(lldb_add_scriptinterpreter_plugin_to_framework name)
+  if(NOT LLDB_BUILD_FRAMEWORK)
+    return()
+  endif()
+  set_property(TARGET ${name} APPEND PROPERTY
+    INSTALL_RPATH "@loader_path/../../..")
+  # Copy under the unversioned name: PluginManager derives a plugin's
+  # initializer symbol from it. A versioned copy would load but never
+  # initialize.
+  set(plugin_in_framework
+    "${LLDB_FRAMEWORK_ABSOLUTE_BUILD_DIR}/LLDB.framework/Versions/${LLDB_FRAMEWORK_VERSION}/$<TARGET_LINKER_FILE_NAME:${name}>")
+  add_custom_command(TARGET ${name} POST_BUILD VERBATIM
+    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy "$<TARGET_FILE:${name}>" "${plugin_in_framework}"
+    COMMENT "Copy ${name} into LLDB.framework")
+  add_custom_target(${name}-framework-cleanup
+    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E remove "${plugin_in_framework}"
+    COMMENT "Removing ${name} from LLDB.framework")
+  add_dependencies(lldb-framework-cleanup ${name}-framework-cleanup)
+endfunction()
+

# Returns TRUE in `out_var` if any of `libs` is `liblldb` or already carries
# the LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB property.
function(_lldb_links_liblldb_check out_var libs)
  set(${out_var} FALSE PARENT_SCOPE)
  foreach(lib ${libs})
    if("${lib}" STREQUAL "liblldb")
      set(${out_var} TRUE PARENT_SCOPE)
      return()
    endif()
    if(TARGET "${lib}")
      get_target_property(_p "${lib}" LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB)
      if(_p)
        set(${out_var} TRUE PARENT_SCOPE)
        return()
      endif()
    endif()
  endforeach()
endfunction()

function(_lldb_propagate_links_liblldb name libs)
  _lldb_links_liblldb_check(_links_liblldb "${libs}")
  set_target_properties(${name} PROPERTIES LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB ${_links_liblldb})
endfunction()

# Records a target's undefined LLDB symbols for re-export by liblldb.
# The output path is appended to the LLDB_DYNAMIC_SCRIPTINTERPRETER_SYMBOL_FILES
# global property.
function(lldb_record_dynamic_script_interpreter_exports target)
  set(symbol_file
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${target}.undefined.symbols")

  # llvm-nm is registered as a CMake target after the LLDB subdirectory is
  # processed, so a forward target reference is required. LLVM_NM, when set,
  # points to a prebuilt host tool for cross-compiled builds.
  if(LLVM_NM)
    set(nm_exe "${LLVM_NM}")
    set(nm_dep)
  else()
    set(nm_exe "$<TARGET_FILE:llvm-nm>")
    set(nm_dep llvm-nm)
  endif()

  set(extra_args)
  if(APPLE)
    list(APPEND extra_args --mach-o)
  endif()

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT ${symbol_file}
    COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
      ${LLDB_SOURCE_DIR}/scripts/extract-dynamic-script-interpreter-exports.py
      --nm ${nm_exe}
      ${extra_args}
      -o ${symbol_file}
      $<TARGET_OBJECTS:${target}>
    DEPENDS
      ${LLDB_SOURCE_DIR}/scripts/extract-dynamic-script-interpreter-exports.py
      $<TARGET_OBJECTS:${target}>
      ${nm_dep}
    COMMAND_EXPAND_LISTS
    VERBATIM
    COMMENT "Extracting LLDB symbols required by ${target}"
  )

  add_custom_target(${target}-exports DEPENDS ${symbol_file})
  set_target_properties(${target}-exports PROPERTIES FOLDER "LLDB/API")

  set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PR

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes XeGPU-to-XeVM matrix-load lowering to derive the LLVM load result type from the active type converter rather than constructing it from the original vector element type. This permits unsupported LLVM element types, such as f8E8M0FNU, to lower to same-width integer storage types and retains scalar lowering for single-element vectors.
Changed symbols: LoadStoreMatrixToXeVMPattern; LLVM::LoadOp; getTypeConverter; convertType
Behavioral change: Matrix-load result types are obtained by converting op.getResult().getType() through the pattern type converter; Non-LLVM-representable element types can lower as converter-selected storage types rather than being used directly as LLVM load element types; Single-element vectors are handled by the converter's scalar result type rather than by an explicit local vector-size branch

Summary: Generalizes SimpleLoopUnswitch's trivial-branch transformation to handle an invariant branch whose selected successor is a loop latch, rather than only a direct loop exit.
